Subject: So this is real. Fernhollow Photo!!

Ok everybody, big work news, and I wanted to tell you before Thanksgiving because I do not have the coordination to make a major life announcement while passing a turkey.

I'm going out on my own. Fernhollow Photo is officially a real business!! My business. Fernhollow Photo LLC, if we're being fancy, which apparently we are because I filled out government paperwork.

I filed the LLC on Oct 22 on my lunch break, sitting in my car outside a Fred Meyer. And then I cried a little. Very glamorous business owner stuff. People buying groceries, me having a whole moment in the parking lot. Anyway. That's where this officially started.

Some of you know I've been shooting for Marisol at Rosebud Lane for the last four years. She told me on Oct 6 that she was closing the studio at the end of October, and Rosebud Lane has now closed. It's a big change. Four years is a lot of weddings and a lot of weekends and a lot of trying to eat something quickly before the next thing happens.

I can't really talk about starting Fernhollow without talking about Marisol, because she basically taught me everything. If you've looked at my pictures over the years and thought, hey, Tessa's getting pretty good at this, a huge amount of that is because of her. She gave me room to learn and trusted me with work that mattered. I'm so grateful I got those four years with her.

She's also referred six of her 2027 couples to me. Having someone who knows your work that well tell people you're the person they should trust with their wedding is a pretty enormous thing. Marisol, if you're reading this someday, thank you. I'll probably say it another 400 times.

Now, before anyone starts quietly assembling a list of jobs with benefits for me: I have been thinking about doing this for two years. This isn't an idea I had three weeks ago and decided to solve by buying a website. The timing changed, but the idea didn't.

And there is actual work on the calendar! I have 14 weddings booked for 2027 already. Six came through Marisol, and eight found me independently. Four are in June, so please remember me fondly during that month. There's also a wedding at Wallowa Lake in September, which I'm really excited about. My camera continues to have a more interesting travel schedule than most people.

The first booking that was completely mine was Dahlia and Ken, June 12 at Timberline. They found me through the pictures I took of one of Marisol's couples at Multnomah Falls. Those pictures made their way to these two people, and those two people decided they wanted ME to photograph their wedding.

I know that's technically how this business works. It still feels a little ridiculous when it happens to you.

My website went live Nov 1. I've got bookings, deposits coming in, and Jae will second shoot the big weddings with me, paid per wedding. So no, I am not planning to somehow stand in two places at once. I have tried that during family photos and it doesn't work.

Dad, this paragraph is specifically for you: health insurance is sorted. I picked a marketplace plan on Nov 5, and it starts Jan 1. I love you. I know why you ask. I also wanted you to have this information before we're all trapped at a table with gravy.

Am I scared? Yes. Obviously. It's my name on the paperwork now, and there's a difference between thinking about something for two years and actually doing it. I'm not going to pretend I suddenly became a person who finds the business side of things relaxing.

But I'm excited, too. Really excited. I've spent four years doing this work, learning it, getting better at it, and finding out that even when my knees are done, I still want to go make the pictures. I have a plan, and I have a pretty good reason to believe I can do this.

Also, the name. Grandma, this part is for you.

Fernhollow is from the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham. That's where I took my first real pictures with your Pentax. Long before wedding timelines and contracts and having opinions about lenses that nobody asked to hear, there was that camera and that trail and you.

I wanted some of that in the name. So when you see Fernhollow Photo, I want you to know it's for you. And yes, now I've made myself cry writing a family blog post. Apparently this is just part of opening a business.

Sam made me a cake to celebrate. It said FERNHOLOW.

One L short, still delicious. We ate it anyway. I appreciate that he has given the business its first unofficial alternate spelling.

Anyway, that's my news!! I wanted you all to hear it from me, and I wanted to have a minute to be happy about it with you before Thanksgiving gets busy.

Mom, yes, Sam is coming. We're bringing rolls and the cranberry thing.

And does anybody want free family pictures while we're at Ruthie's? I'll bring the camera. Let me know so we can grab some daylight before dinner. New babies, whole families, whoever wants in.

Uncle Greg, we'll try to be quick. Grandma, wear whatever sweater you want properly documented.

Love you all. I'm scared and happy and apparently a business owner. See you at Thanksgiving!!
